eventMetadata.context_description: Official Korea Meteorological Administration forecasts for August 13 point to a daytime maximum near 33°C in the Seoul-Incheon area under mostly clear to partly cloudy skies, with overnight lows around 24°C and only modest precipitation chances. Recent model guidance and surface observations show a weakening heat ridge after early-August extremes above 40°C elsewhere in South Korea, leaving modest uncertainty around peak insolation, boundary-layer mixing, and any late-day sea-breeze effects from Incheon that could trim the maximum by 1–2°C. With 31°C and 32°C together commanding over 80% of market-implied probability, traders appear to be weighting the narrow gap between the official outlook and possible slight cooling from increased cloud cover or timing of the daily peak. Updated KMA briefings and afternoon model runs will be the next key inputs before resolution.
